paper_name: Global EDF Scheduling of Directed Acyclic Graphs on Multiprocessor Systems
paper_description: Provides a tighter workload and interference analysis for G-EDF scheduling of sporadic constrained-deadline DAG tasks on homogeneous multiprocessors by assigning local offsets and deadlines to subtasks, deriving an improved sufficient schedulability test and studying its sustainability.

formal_description.statement: A sporadic DAG task tau_i = (T_i, D_i, G_i) where G_i = (V_i, E_i) is a DAG with vertices V_i subtasks, edges E_i precedences; each v in V_i has C_v execution time; jobs released every T_i, deadline D_i <= T_i.
formal_description.conclusion: Models parallel tasks with internal structure for global scheduling

informal_sketch.intuition: Captures parallelism and dependencies in real-time tasks via graph.
steps: Define graph G_i with subtasks V_i and edges E_i
Sporadic releases with period T_i, deadline D_i

formal_description.statement: For subtask v in tau_i, assign o_v local offset, d_v local deadline s.t. 0 <= o_v <= d_v <= D_i, respecting precedences: for (u,v) in E_i, d_u + C_v <= d_v.
formal_description.conclusion: Decomposes task deadline to subtasks for analysis

informal_sketch.intuition: Breaks down global deadline to local constraints for tighter bounds.
steps: Propagate: d_v = min(D_i, min_{pred u} d_u + C_v)

formal_description.statement: Task tau_i schedulable under G-EDF if forall t in [0, D_i], sum_{j=1 to n} W_j(t) <= m * t, where W_j(t) is workload bound using local offsets/deadlines.
formal_description.conclusion: Sufficient schedulability test via improved DBF

informal_sketch.intuition: Demand <= supply using refined per-subtask bounds.
steps: Compute local o_v, d_v for all subtasks
DBF_j(t) = sum_v min(C_v, max(0, t - o_v)) for jobs in window
Check sum DBF <= m*t for all t
